nodes.text: Estimate $n_k$, the smallest integer $>2k$ such that $\prod_{1\leq i\leq k}(n_k-i)$ has no prime factor in $(k,2k)$.

#451 : [Er79d,p.78] [ErGr80,p.89] number theory Erdős and Graham write 'we can prove $n_k>k^{1+c}$ but no doubt much more is true'. In [Er79d] Erdős writes that probably $n_k<e^{o(k)}$ but $n_k>k^d$ for all constant $d$. Adenwalla observes that an easy upper bound is $n_k\leq \prod_{k<p<2k}p=e^{O(k)}$. van Doorn and Tang [vDTa26] (using an argument generated by GPT 5.5 Pro and Tang) have proved that\[n_k> \exp\left(c\frac{(\log k)^2}{\log\log k}\right)\]for some constant $c>0$. See also [1095] .
